summary: Set 111 Session 4: the ceremony pass, plus the remediation that made it true. Shipped the authoring-time session-size cap (ai_router.spec_admission, threshold MEASURED from 172 v4 sessions: 6+ steps doubles median session time), the canonical test-run policy with an EXECUTABLE freshness gate (ai_router.run_of_record + check_test_run_fresh, which reproduces and refuses the Set 110 S3 stale-run pattern), the guided-look UAT format with a fail-closed close gate (check_uat_walk_recorded: a requiresUAT session closes only with its walk or an operator-attested waiver), the walk stager (npm run walk), ai_router.session_checklist (operator-directed step-level progress for every consumer repo), and CI hygiene (all 31 workflow uses: pinned to 40-char SHAs, dependabot.yml, a drift_guard actions-sha-pinned check). The artifact table, admission bar and close-backstop bound went to the operator as a batched education-mode brief; all three defaults were taken and journaled. Verification then found the ceremony pass had shipped its centrepiece broken: the walk stager could never have worked. The reveal lived in the product extension's activate(), which only runs once the Dabbler view is visible -- so it was waiting on the event it was supposed to cause, and the only tests were source-text greps asserting the line existed. Eight blocking findings across two discovery passes; six real defects fixed, one rejected on evidence. The reveal moved to a development-only walk companion (scripts/walk-companion/, onStartupFinished), leaving no walk-specific code in the product and its Set 110 activation profile untouched; npm run walk:smoke now PROVES the reveal by reading a marker the companion writes after the command resolves. scripts/vscode-launch.js became the genuine single definition of binary discovery and Electron env hygiene -- it had re-implemented both from an old copy of the harness, dropping the macOS .app-bundle search (npm run walk was broken on every Mac) and the IPC-variable allowlist (a walk started from VS Code's own terminal could parse args instead of opening). run_of_record normalised paths with os.sep, a no-op on posix, so the package's own test was red on the required ubuntu/macOS matrix while green here. The UAT gate had a hole shaped like its own purpose: an omitted uatScope collapsed to 'none' and disarmed it, so requiresUAT: true with no scope -- the likeliest hand-authored shape -- was exactly the spec that could close with no walk; scope now chooses WHICH sessions owe a walk and never cancels the requirement. The Layer 3 freshness map named only two of the policy's four trigger surfaces and now covers the blessed state-file writers and the fixture/walk harness. Finding 8 (the pypa publish pin allegedly on a moving branch) was REJECTED on API evidence: v1.14.2 is an annotated tag that dereferences to exactly the pinned commit, and all six workflow pins were verified to match their tags. Runs of record after code freeze: pytest 3,801 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped; Layer 3 Playwright 33 passed. Layer 2 mocha gained 10 tests (1,876 passing) against an unchanged 32-failure pre-existing baseline caused by VS Code 1.132 making workspace.workspaceFolders getter-only -- measured on a clean tree, recorded as a residual, deliberately not repaired under remediation pressure. Finally, at the UAT stop the operator asked whether narrated video walkthroughs are possible; a controlled experiment showed Playwright's recordVideo BREAKS the automation it would record while the same launch without it drives the real UI fine, and Set 113 was authored (proposal + spec + state, all three sessions inside the 5-step cap this session shipped) to be run after Set 112.

uat.attestation:
Operator-attested waiver, 2026-08-08. The walk was NOT performed, and the reason is the deliverable itself rather than schedule pressure. This session's guided-look format -- a document of Look items driven from a terminal -- is the format the operator has repeatedly found unusable: "I want to do UAT, but the experience has to be good. In the past, it has been awful... the instructions have been way too difficult to decipher and often too involved. Often, the setup is too involved." Walking it would have produced a judgment on a format already superseded by decision.

What this session DID fix is the staging half of that cost, and that part is proven rather than attested: `npm run walk` stages a disposable workspace, an isolated Extension Development Host, and the revealed Dabbler view in one command, and `npm run walk:smoke` reports `PASS: revealed` -- an executable check the session was required to invent because verification caught the original walk stager silently never revealing anything at all.

The comprehension half is now Set 113 (docs/session-sets/113-narrated-video-walkthroughs/), authored this session on operator instruction and sequenced after Set 112: narrated video walkthroughs with an optional 'repeat it yourself' manual walkthrough rendered from the same source. Whether watching a video can satisfy requiresUAT is explicitly reserved there as an operator-held decision under the verification-reduction carve-out -- this waiver does not pre-decide it.

Recorded as a waiver, visibly, which is the outcome the Set 111 S4 gate exists to force: skipping is now a decision on the record rather than an evaporation.
